rounds.text: Northlink Fiscal & Capital Services Ltd is currently trading at a precarious valuation, with a P/E ratio of 96.4x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 42.05x, which significantly exceeds the sector benchmark of 13.08x [E11]. This optimism is disconnected from the company’s long-term performance, as evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -14% [E14] and a 5-year compounded profit growth of -8% [E19]. The stock is trading at a substantial premium to its intrinsic value, with a DCF analysis suggesting an intrinsic value of only Rs 4 per share against a market price of Rs 25.7, resulting in a margin of safety of -575% [E37, E38]. Furthermore, the company’s historical profitability remains weak, characterized by a 3-year median return on equity of -5% [E28] and a current ROE of only 2.4% [E13]. Conceded: the company has shown recent improvement with 150% sales growth and 123% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21], and promoters have increased their stake by 10.96 percentage points [E34]. However, the exit of domestic institutional investors, who reduced their holding from 25.26% to 0.00%, signals a significant lack of confidence from professional market participants [E35].
